newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar settles down, nearby switch grows.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar settles down, nearby switch grows.

text.p: CSCE sugar futures closed an active session weaker Friday as speculators continued to roll spot July contracts into the back months ahead of first notice day, traders said.
July futures expire Monday. Open interest remained high as of Thursday at 17,353 lots, down 6,744 lots. Open interest in October stood at 91,398 lots.
"The large open interest in October has people concerned that something dramatic is going to happen," Tony Passimenti, a sugar broker with Merrill Lynch, said.

But sources said today's losses reflect a gradual retreat from recent highs, rather than a massive sell-off. Steady fund buying and scale-down buying by the trade held October sugar over 11.00 cents a lb, dealers said.
"We keep eroding the market day by day, point by point. Everybody is not runnng for the door at the same time," Passimenti said.
Benchmark October should find firm support at 11.00 cents, followed by the recent low of 10.96 cents and then at 10.80 cents.
The spot month closed 0.19 cent lower at 10.92 cents, traded 11.13 to 10.91 cents. Most-active October settled 0.11 cent weaker at 11.14 cents, while the outer months settled 0.03 to 0.07 cent lower.
Traders blamed losses on speculative selling in the nearby switch, which triggered stops at 11.22 cents in October and knocked the benchmark contract to the day's lows.
The July/October switch ended at 0.22 cent premium October, compared with 0.14 on Thursday.
The large open interest in the July contract is expected to fall to abound 7,000 lots by Monday, market sources said.
An estimated 35,542 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Thursday's official 19,710 lots.
Technical resistance in October remained at 11.34 cents, followed by 11.42 cents in October.
